Phase 1: The Pre-Flight Safety Check
Before you throw supplements or antimicrobials at your gut, check your nervous system and your bile, the mechanics they need to work.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
Hale (Kick Your Fat in the Nuts) and Stanley Rosenberg (Accessing the Healing Power of the Vagus Nerve).
Are your pupils dilated all the time? Are you missing your gag reflex?

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
Then according to Hale, you're stuck in fight or flight mode (which in medical lingo is called "sympathetic dominance"), and digestion is offline. Rosenberg's fix is his Basic Exercise (eye movements) or the Salamander technique (which looks like some kind of yoga, see a video demo here). Both of those help to mechanically release the vagus nerve so your body can switch into rest and digest mode.
Now let's have a look at your bile function.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Do you burp extra (not just like one little burp) after fatty meals? Do your stools float (like it's hard to flush), or look like clay?

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Then your bile is stagnant (not flowing well), and Hale says if you take antimicrobials now, you'll get a herx reaction: the dying microbes release toxins you can't detoxify.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: So thin the bile first with Beet Flow (an extract of beet greens) or phosphatidylcholine, a fatty nutrient found in egg yolks and soy, before starting on any pathogen killing protocol.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: My notes: for stress and sleep see "Severe stress" above, and for stomach acid and bile see "Low stomach acid".

Optional Ready-Made Gut Stacks
I don't think there's one supplement stack (a set of supplements you take together) that heals everyone's gut, and no stack can do the phases above for you. So do those first, in order, and only go after bugs and parasites if your symptoms are still there after you've changed your diet. Then a stack can help with the rebuilding in Phase 5, once you're clear of infection and it's time to feed the good bacteria again.
Look for a stack that covers these 3 categories:
First, your gut needs its good bacteria back, so take a probiotic that's easy on your stomach.
Then keep them fed with a prebiotic, the kind of fiber they eat, and take something that helps them make short-chain fatty acids, especially the main one, butyrate, or take butyrate itself.
Last, something to help your gut lining heal, like glutamine, zinc carnosine, colostrum, or herbs that soothe it.
